findings.title: remove() unconditionally hits the DB to fetch the IDP
findings.body: The diff hoists `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` out of the `if (isInvalid(cacheKey))` branch so the result can be passed to the new `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)` call. As a consequence, every `remove(alias)` now performs a JPA `getByAlias` lookup, even when the IDP is fully cached in `CachedIdentityProvider`. Previously the DB was only hit on the invalidation path or on a cache miss; the cache-hit path was DB-free. The login-eligibility check can be satisfied by reusing the cached model (e.g. `cached != null ? cached.getIdentityProvider() : idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)`), so this regression is avoidable without losing the new invalidation behaviour.

findings.title: searchKey for REALM_ONLY mode varies with organizationId unnecessarily
findings.body: In `getForLogin`, `String searchKey = organizationId != null ? organizationId : "";` is used for every `FetchMode`, but `FetchMode.REALM_ONLY` does not depend on `organizationId` (the default implementation always sets `ORGANIZATION_ID` to null for that mode, so the result set is identical regardless of the orgId parameter). Calls to `getForLogin(REALM_ONLY, ...)` with different non-null organizationIds will miss the searchKey inside the cached `IdentityProviderListQuery`, fall into the `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)`/re-query path, and accumulate redundant searchKeys in the same cached entry. The searchKey for `REALM_ONLY` should be a constant (e.g. always `""`) so all REALM_ONLY lookups share one cached entry.
